description: A bright, airy dining room adjacent to a kitchen, photographed at standing eye-level with a normal lens around 35mm, in a three-quarter corner composition that captures both the dining zone and the kitchen beyond a large arched doorway. The ceiling is a vaulted cathedral with exposed natural bleached oak timber beams and white-painted tongue-and-groove shiplap planks filling the panels between, giving the space a relaxed coastal or Hamptons character. The arched doorway through to the kitchen is a generous smooth-plastered round-topped arch. The kitchen visible beyond features white painted cabinetry, a marble slab backsplash, a reeded-front light oak island with a marble countertop, and a bright multi-pane window flooding the space with daylight. Back in the dining room, a large round light oak pedestal dining table is surrounded by six upholstered dining chairs in natural linen with a skirted base and loose cushion seat; two arm chairs at the table ends have a slightly more formal presence. On the table, a large cream ceramic jug-vase and a low wooden bowl filled with round wooden objects serve as simple centerpiece styling. A floor-to-ceiling light oak cabinet with flat panel doors and small knobs stands against the back wall. On the kitchen pass-through counter is a large grey stoneware vase of significant height, a piece of coastal artwork in soft blue-grey tones, and a coral specimen. The floor is wide-plank light oak. The palette is entirely composed of cream, warm white, and natural sandy oak tones — serene, coastal, understated.
